newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: C-C Amatil sprints 11 pct higher on deal.
newsitem.headline: C-C Amatil sprints 11 pct higher on deal.

text.p: Shares in Australian-based bottling group Coca Cola Amatil Ltd bolted A$1.45 or 11.3 percent higher to A$14.25 in opening trade on Friday on further positive reaction to its A$3.4 billion soft drink merger deal with the Philippines' San Miguel Corp announced on Thursday.

Under the surprise agreement, C-C Amatil would issue 293 million shares to acquire San Miguel soft drink subsidiary Coca Cola Bottler Philippines Inc (CCBPI), which is owned 70 percent by San Miguel and 30 percent by The Cola Cola Co.
C-C Amatil chairman Dean Wills said the Philippines deal would add immediately to the company's earnings and growth prospects, strengthen its balance sheet and improve earnings per share.
Brokers said the market had welcomed the deal, which appeared to end a run of bad news for the stock.

Intersuisse head of equities Andrew Sekely said the jump in C-C Amatil had to be seen in the context of its sharp fall from grace over the preceeding six months from around A$18 on earnings disappointments.
"A very good stock was really needing a bit of a blood transfusion and the market perceives that it's got that with this deal," Sekely said.
"It's a combination of some lucky people who sold at higher prices coming back in and others who bought at higher prices maybe averaging a little bit," he said.
"The perception is that they have laid the groundwork for a return to better times."
Brokers said, however, C-C Amatil's run higher may have run out of steam for the moment, as there remained some pessimists on the stock.

"It's a twin edged sword, with positive comments and some negatives, so it's one camp or the other and it looks like the buyers are winning," Burdett, Buckridge and Young broker Stephen Smith said as the stock rose sharply in the first half hour.
Sekely said he thought the stock may be overbought at its current levels.
By 11.05 a.m. (0105 GMT), C-C Amatil had eased back to A$13.90, but was still up A$1.10 on Thursday's close.
